card.headline: Amina is carrying an adjusted share of 70.48 while Farah carries 48.33, a 22-point gap against a circle mean of 62.67.
what_i_tried: Moved the overnight stay, weekend visit, and both medication tasks from Amina to Rian to shift 855 weighted minutes off the highest carrier
Moved the Saturday overnight stay, Friday medication task, and two other permitted tasks from Amina to Rian to consolidate weekend work
Attempted two other configurations that transferred Amina's heaviest movable tasks to Rian
Each move made the deviation worse, so none were kept
card.the_tension: Every task that might move from Amina to Farah is blocked by stated limits. Farah refuses night shifts, which rules out the two overnight stays. Farah is unavailable Friday and Saturday, which rules out the weekend visit and the Friday medication task. The only sibling who can receive tasks from Amina is Rian, but every attempted move in that direction made the overall split less proportional. The gap cannot close within the limits on record.

options.label: Leave the split as it stands
options.consequence: Amina continues carrying a significantly higher adjusted share than Farah. All three siblings accepted their assignments, but the proportionality gap remains outside tolerance.

options.label: Bring in paid help for the Wednesday overnight stay and Friday nephrology appointment
options.consequence: Those two tasks come off the family schedule. The fairness tools show this would bring the worst deviation to 0.129, within tolerance.

options.label: Talk it through as a family
options.consequence: You may find a solution I cannot see, such as one sibling revisiting a limit or adjusting declared capacity. That conversation belongs to you.

card.what_i_will_not_decide: I hold the stated limits and compute proportionality, but I do not decide whether paid help is worth the cost, whether anyone should reconsider a boundary, or whether an imperfect split is good enough this month. Those choices require judgment about your mother's needs, your family's resources, and what each of you is carrying outside this plan. That judgment is yours, not mine.

card.headline: Paid help could cover 2 of this month's tasks. Whether to bring someone in is your decision, not mine.
what_i_tried: Looked for moves between you that stay inside everyone's stated limits.
Found that paid help for Wednesday overnight stay (Wed 14 Oct); Follow-up nephrology appointment (Fri 23 Oct) would take 11.5 hours of care off Amina and Rian.
card.the_tension: The worst deviation would go from 23 percent to 13 percent, against a limit of 15 percent. It also means spending money, and someone new in Nasrin's home.

options.label: Bring in paid help for these tasks
options.consequence: The spread goes from 23 percent to 13 percent. You agree between you who pays, and Nasrin has a say in it. I will arrange the same each month until you say otherwise.

options.label: Keep this care within the family
options.consequence: Nothing changes. The current split stands, and I will not suggest paid help again.

card.what_i_will_not_decide: Whether to pay for care, who pays, and whether someone new comes into Nasrin's home. Those choices belong to your family, and to Nasrin.
